```{python}
# Load data

# this function cleans up the weird column name formatting SQLAlchemy addes to the df when loading. 
def load_table(table_name, engine):
    df = pd.read_sql_table(table_name, engine)
    df.columns = [str(col) for col in df.columns]
    return df

dc_df = load_table("naics_518_establishments", engine)
air_df = load_table("air_quality", engine)
bus_df = load_table("business_patterns", engine)
gdp_df = load_table("gdp", engine)
inc_df = load_table("personal_income", engine)
pop_df = load_table("population", engine)
perm_df = load_table("res_construction_permits", engine)
emp_df = load_table("unemployment", engine)
county_df = load_table("us_counties", engine)
```

```{python}
# log all columns with lots of outliers
cols_to_log = list(set(mega_df.columns) - set(mlu.column_selector(mega_df, False, -1, 3, False, False)))

def log_cols(df, cols_to_log):
    for col in cols_to_log:
        df[col] = df[col].replace(0,1e-9) #logging a zero causes -inf
        df[f"{col}_logged"] = np.log(df[col])
        df = df.drop(columns=[col])
    return df

df_logged = log_cols(mega_df, cols_to_log)
```

```{python}

```

### K-Nearest Neighbor

```{python}
# Range of k values to try
k_range = range(1, 75)
cv_scores = []

# Evaluate each k using 5-fold cross-validation
for k in k_range:
    knn = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=k)
    scores = cross_val_score(knn, X_scaled, y, cv=5, scoring='accuracy')
    cv_scores.append(scores.mean())

# Plot accuracy vs. k
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.plot(k_range, cv_scores, marker='o')
plt.title("k-NN Cross-Validation Accuracy vs k")
plt.xlabel("Number of Neighbors: k")
plt.ylabel("Cross-Validated Accuracy")
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# Best k
best_k = k_range[np.argmax(cv_scores)]
print(f"Best k from cross-validation: {best_k}")
```

```{python}
# Train a k-NN classifier
knn = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=68)
knn.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Predict and evaluate
y_pred = knn.predict(X_test)
mlu.model_accuracy_report(knn,X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test)
```

KNN accuracy is decent, but not particuarly enlightening since it does not reduce dimentionality and thus does not allow us to visuzual and explore the data like PCA or UMAP. 



### K Means Clustering

The hypothesis is that using this unsupervised ML model will help us uncover meaningful groupings in our data. Perhaps we find that there are 3 distinct types of counties which we can then test via linear regression to see if their responses to additional datacenters are the same or different. 


```{python}
df = mega_df
df = log_cols(mega_df, cols_to_log)

selected_cols = mlu.column_selector(df, False, -1, 4, False, False)
df_trimmed_cols = df[selected_cols]
df_trimmed_cols = df_trimmed_cols.dropna()

X = df_trimmed_cols.drop(columns = [
    "has_datacenter",
    "centroid_lon",
    "centroid_lat",
    "county_id",
    "civilian_labor_force_logged",
    "pm25_pop_daily_avg_logged",
    "pm25_mean_daily_avg_logged",
    "multifamily_permits_2_units_per_capita_logged",
    "multifamily_permits_3_4_units_per_capita_logged",
    "multifamily_permits_5_or_more_units_per_capita_logged"])
y = df_trimmed_cols['has_datacenter']

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_scaled, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)
```


```{python}
# check performance of clustering model 
scores = {}
for k in range(2, 50):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=42)
    labels = km.fit_predict(X_train)
    scores[k] = silhouette_score(X_train, labels)

# Plot scores
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4))
plt.plot(list(scores.keys()), list(scores.values()), marker='o')
plt.xlabel('Number of Clusters (k)')
plt.ylabel('Silhouette Score')
plt.title('Silhouette Score vs. k')
plt.show()
```
Higher Silhouette scores indicate better separate bewetween clusters and thus better performance. Score ranges from -1 to 1

```{python}
# choose number of cluters to use
n_clusters=3
```

```{python}
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters, init='k-means++', max_iter=300, n_init=10, random_state=42)

kmeans.fit(X_train)

cluster_labels = kmeans.predict(X_train)

```

```{python}
# Check which featurs are contributing most to cluster separation
X_train_df = pd.DataFrame(X_train, columns=X.columns)
X_train_df['Cluster'] = cluster_labels

# Calculate cluster means
cluster_means = X_train_df.groupby('Cluster').mean()

# Plot heatmap with  feature names
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))
sns.heatmap(
    cluster_means.T, 
    cmap='coolwarm', 
    annot=True, 
    fmt='.2f'
)

plt.title('Cluster Profiles by Feature Means')
plt.xlabel('Cluster ID')
plt.ylabel('Features')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

silhouette_avg_train_data = silhouette_score(X_train, cluster_labels)
print(f'Train Data Silhouette Score: {silhouette_avg_train_data:.2f}')

test_cluster_labels = kmeans.predict(X_test)
silhouette_avg_test = silhouette_score(X_test, test_cluster_labels)
print(f'Test Data Silhouette Score: {silhouette_avg_test:.2f}')
```


```{python}
# save cluster lables to data frame for later use
train_clusters = kmeans.predict(X_train)
test_clusters = kmeans.predict(X_test)

kmeans_labled_df = df_trimmed_cols.copy()

kmeans_labled_df.loc[y_train.index, 'cluster_label'] = train_clusters
kmeans_labled_df.loc[y_test.index, 'cluster_label'] = test_clusters

kmeans_labled_df['cluster_label'] = kmeans_labled_df['cluster_label'].astype(int)
```
